column1: NOTICE: The Chancellor of Thaermore has officially closed the gateway to Crakamir and the southern trade routes until further notice.
waiting room

Long ago, there were only the great ones- the Darkness, named Onos, and the Light, named Rai. They fought for control of the sky, but it was Onos who dominated and kept Rai away, exiled far beyond the most distant stars. In this time, Darkness reigned supreme.

But Rai schemed to dethrone Onos and so gathered an army of burning comets for which to attack the darkness. From the black abyss of the most distant realm, Rai moved with his army and surprised Onos, driving back darkness and bringing light to the sky.

Onos, in all his wickedness, retaliated with great vengeance! In an act of madness, he punched a hole in the sky to consume all of the comets, but their numbers were too great. As all of the cosmos began falling into this hole, the comets came crashing together and formed a single brilliant gem, too large to be pulled through the opening. The gem became known as Eschalon, and its greatness alone was enough to seal the hole formed by Onos.

With the immense pull created by Eschalon and the remnant hole, Onos and Rai were dragged into an endless spiral from which they could not escape. Ever spinning around Eschalon, they gave the land its first day and night, which has continued for endless millennia since. Their imprisonment became the gift of all the creatures of Eschalon.
Welcome to the Underground Repository. Validation required for entry. House rules strictly enforced. Trespassers will become permanent guests of the Repository.

...would not be recommended under any circumstances. However, one would find that equal parts Willow Sap as a reagent, and Sulfur as a reactant, produces the most effective form of healing elixir. With many years of practice, the talented Alchemist can craft elixirs with properties exceeding that of even...

After scouting several different areas, I think the pit area is the best place to store my valuables until order is restored in this region. The Salamanders won't disturb the chests and everyone knows best to stay away from this area. Yes! I think the Salamanders will make perfect guards! The invisibility potion will keep me hidden from the beasts until I am finished stashing me belongings...it is common knowledge that Salamanders hunt using sight, not smell. Or is it the other way around? No matter, it will only take me a few moments to place the chests.
Deconstructing Portals and Gateways

and settle into this new life. If you choose the path of truth it will be a hard and dangerous journey. *And so, if the truth is what you seek, you need to start by retrieving an amulet that belongs to you. Before your memory was taken, you requested that I secure a special amulet for you. I did so by slipping it into the coffin of a recently deceased aristocrat named

. He is interred in a vault at Eversleep Cemetery in the North Parish region. I knew his casket would be a secure place to hide your amulet; the problem now is retrieving it. The door to the crypt is locked tight. Smashing the door down or picking the lock might be an option, but it may be easiest to just get the key. The cemetery director, Leurik, lives a bit north of Aridell and he has the key. I am confident that you could figure out a way to get it from him. *Once you retrieve your amulet from the crypt, take it to a woman named Lilith who lives in Tangletree Forest. Look for her house in the
natural casting
Temporal Linking
Foozgrumph
With the Crux back in our possession we now have the power to reclaim our ancient homelands. You've aided the race of Goblins, and now I make good on my offer.

Take this gold, human. It is enough to buy passage out of Thaermore where you can retire as a wealthy lord. But heed this warning: once you leave this Citadel you will be just another human to us. Leave Thaermore and never return.
Great Underground
The Crux of Ages
The Great One
Goblin Clans of Thaermore
Clan leader
The Orakur are watching!
Three-fingered Sam's Guide to making Demon Oil
I don't like visitors, so make this quick.
I am looking for a man named Maddock. Are you him, by any chance?
Why yes, that is me.
Hey! I believe I am expecting you. Your name is $, isn't it? I have something for you.
Yes, I'm glad I have found you. I was given a strange note and was told I needed to locate you. I hope you can make sense of this confusion.
I don't know if I can help you with your confusion, but I do have a letter and some gold that I was told to hold for you. I've kept it in the chest over there. You can fetch it yourself.
I'm very sorry to disturb you, but I was hoping you could answer some questions for me.

Eh, I don't know much about the comings and goings in this village because I pretty much keep to myself, but I'd be glad to chat a bit with you. I guess it is nice to have a visitor, even an uninvited one.
I'm sorry for intruding. Pardon me.
I appreciate that you've kept these items secure for me. Who asked you to do this?

Who? Well, I don't know really. I try not to get too involved with other people's business. Years ago I was a courier for Lord Archable, so people have always just entrusted me with important matters. A gentleman came to town a while back and paid me to do this job for him- to hold on to these items for someone with your name fitting your description. He wore a mask and I wasn't able to see his face. I didn't ask who he was or why he needed this done. It's the Courier's Code not to ask questions.
Thank you very much. I wish I had time to chat a bit, but I must be going.
You're not from around here, eh? Well, we're at war with the Orakur of course!
You don't know where you are?  Well, you're in the village of Aridell, in the Parishes region of Thaermore.
You're just going to have to ask around.
But I'm telling you there's not much in the way of jobs around here, 'specially for some stranger new in town.
I'd like to ask you something else.

Yes, the Orakur- those thieving creatures that live underground! They can't be trusted! If you ask me, our forefathers should have wiped them out when they first arrived, then we wouldn't be in this mess. I am glad the current Chancellor has the fortitude to stand up to them and make them pay for their crimes.

Eh, I'm just a tired old man and I don't really follow any of this political nonsense anyway. If you want to know more about it, you're going to have to ask someone else. Eleanor at the council house knows a lot about this subject.
Hey! What are you doing here? You can't just barge into someone's house without being invited! I suggest you turn and leave before I teach you a lesson in manners you won't soon forget!
Son, did you just fall off a boat? Yes, you're in Thaermore. If you are really this lost then you need to find yourself a map. I'd give you mine if I had one.
Can I ask you another question?
What can I do for you, blessed traveler?
Thank you for inquiring about our healing services.
I am cursed and need spiritual restoration.
Thank you for inquiring about our dehexification services.
Can you answer some questions for me, Father?

My child, if you are seeking answers to your spiritual questions, you only need to look inside yourself first. Then pray. Only after hours and hours of prayer and meditation will you find what you are seeking.
Welcome to the Bethel of the Green Moon, weary traveler! My name is Father Michael. Here at the Bethel we can heal your wounds and restore your soul, for a small donation of course.
Uh, well that's not really what I meant.

Then you should rid yourself of your material possessions. They will bring you nothing but misery. The true path to enlightenment is through temperance and humility. I'll remind you that the church always accepts donations.
I was hoping the Bethel would have some work for me.
The Bethel always has work for people wishing to serve the Will of Luna, although you don't earn gold for doing these jobs- you earn honor which is much more valuable!

I have been told of a destitute man living west of the Salted Coast region, which is a coastal area south of here. He has contracted Fleshrot and is in need of healing. The Bethel has a very rare potion of Absolute Restoration that needs to be delivered to him so that he can be rid of his debilitating illness, but unfortunately the Salted Coast area has become very dangerous and no one has been able to complete this task.

Remember, if you accept this mission you'll receive no financial payment for your efforts. This would be an act of pure selflessness on your behalf. Are you willing to perform this task for the Bethel?
I am sorry you feel that way. Perhaps one day you'll find that helping others is itself a reward greater than gold. May the light show you the way, my son.
Okay, I will perform this task for you.

Wonderful! You may retreive the potion from the chest here in the Bethel. Remember, you must be very careful in the Salted Coast region. Since the war began, the Commonwealth Guard withdrew from the area and it has fallen under control by pirates, thugs and cutpurses.
Yes, ah, you don't know about this war with the Orakur? Maybe you had better talk to Eleanor, Aridell's Council Head about that.
And don't forget the potion on your way out!
Can I show you something from my inventory?
Yes, I'd like to see what you have for sale.
Thank you for your patronage.
Actually, I was hoping you might have some work for me. I'm a bit short on gold.

Looking for work, eh? Sure, I have something for you: I used to own a house down in Elderhollow, before the village was attacked and we were forced to leave. Beneath my house I had a wine cellar where I kept some of the precious metals I use in my smithing work. When I fled the village I took with me all I could, but I left behind a single bar of Mithril that was hidden deep inside the cellar. Now it's far too dangerous for me to try to recover the Mithril myself, and it's too valuable just to leave it down there for thieves to eventually take.

If you could recover this bar of Mithril for me, I'd pay you a reward worth the face value of the raw metal. Before you agree, let me warn you: this was no ordinary wine cellar. I filled it with traps designed to keep theives away, and by now I'm sure there are things more dangerous than traps down there. It won't be a simple task.
So what do you say? Are you up for an adventure?
Sounds like a good time to me! I'll do it.
Excellent! I look forward to your return with the Mithril.
No way. I'm not going to risk my life for a chunk of metal.
Well, I don't blame you at all. It's a job probably more suited for a brash, adventurer-type person seeking glory and riches, not people like you and me.
Thank you very much! I had my doubts that you'd be able to retrieve it, but I was wrong.
This bar of Mithril is valued at 375 gold, so I'll give you full price for it. You deserve it!
I risked my life for that chunk of metal. I think you owe me a little more than 375 gold...
Is that right? Well sir, we had a deal, and I was even being generous given the state of things around here. If you think I owe you something more, you're going to have to come and take it from me!
Hail, my name is Farwick, owner of this metalworks shop. Can I show you something from my current stock?
Are you in need of some magickal supplies?
I usually get some new stuff in every few days, so come back and have another look at my inventory soon!
I'm not from around here. Can you tell me anything about this area?

There's not much to tell you, really. The conflict with the Orakur has left this region in a state of chaos. Our little village of Aridell is really the last settlement still standing in eastern Thaermore. The other settlements are gone and most people have fled north, or west before Grimmhold fell. Out here, so far from the Capital, we know very little about what's really going on.
I'm looking for work. Do you have anything for me?

No, I don't need any help around the store. However, I am looking for a special book called 'Secrets of Transference Circuits'. I would certainly pay you full value for that book if you ever found a copy and returned it to me.
Sorry, I don't have time to find books for you.
That's alright. You look like the type of man who normally avoids books anyways.
Oh! Thank you so much. I've been searching for this book ever since my last copy was destroyed in a fire. As promised, here's your payment.
So, you're that kind of person, are you? Fine. I don't want any trouble, so here's another 50 gold then. Take it and be gone.
Hail! Welcome to the Grand Magicks Emporium! I'm Abygale, proprietor of this shop of magicks and magickal supplies. Can I show you something from my current inventory?
Please, can you tell me more about this conflict?

I'm sorry, I don't really know much about it other than it has to do with the theft of a gemstone. I personally think it is absurd that so many lives have been lost over such a trival matter. This war is about nothing more than the pride of the Chancellor. If you really want to know more about it you should go speak to our Council Head, Eleanor Mistlepine, though I suspect she'll just give you the patriotic speach she gives everyone.
Can you tell me about this 'Grimmhold' place?

Grimmhold is an old fortress which lies just a short walk west of here. It once served as a gateway between this area and western Thaermore, cutting a swath through the thickest part of Tangletree Forest. It also bridges the Eastern Gap, a huge rift cut into the ground that lies in the center of the forest.

After the conflict began, the Commonwealth Guards who held Grimmhold were called to service by the Chancellor. Soon after their departure, Goblins overran and took control of the fortress. It fell, just like Elderhollow southwest of here.

Yes! Vile creatures, those Goblins are. In the past they've posed little threat to us humans, but with our resources spread thin and our attention focused on the conflict with the Orakur, they've taken advantage of the situation and now run amok. In my opinion their taking of Grimmhold is just the start. If the Chancellor doesn't change his war plan they are going to become a bigger threat than the Orakur!

Grimmhold is now unsafe and probably not even passable. If you absolutely must travel west, you should take the northern pass. Unfortunately, this is a much longer journey and probably just as dangerous- but I guess it's safer than trying to go around Tangletree Forest to the south. The southern route is plagued with bandits.

No one knows really.They are called underfolk; beings that live in perpetual darkness underground and have inhabited this region far longer than us humans have. Practically everything I have ever heard about them come from legends and wives' tales. Before this war most people thought of the Orakur as nothing more than spooky creatures that were told to children in bedtime stories. Whatever they are, they must be fierce warriors- the Chancellor has called every Guard from eastern Thaermore into service, leaving us out here to defend ourselves.
You mentioned a place called Grimmhold. What is that?
Thank you for taking time to chat with me.
What can I help you with?
Do you have time to answer some questions for me?
Certainly!
What is your question?

Oh yes. Maddock is an elderly gentleman who lives just down the street southeast of here. He lives in a small house on the other side of the Bethel of the Green Moon. He's a bit of a codgery old man, not too fond of visitors.
I woke up in an abandoned house southwest of here and I don't know where I am!
Southwest, you say? It sounds like you just came from Elderhollow, a nearby village that was ruined a few years ago.
Porter, the owner of the Owl's Roost Tavern, sells miscellaneous supplies. He may have a regional map of the area if you think that would help you.
I've seen many strange beasts roaming around outside the village and ruined buildings. What has happened to this land?
You must be from far outside Thaermore if you are unaware of the events in this region!
Well, this land is embroiled in a war that we are currently fighting with the Orakur. What you see out there, the beasts that roam the land and the ruins, are all remnants of this war.
I need supplies. Can you tell me a bit about your town?

Of course! This is my office where I conduct the village's business. Next door is the Bethel of the Green Moon, run by Father Micahel, who offers healing services. Up the street to the northeast you'll find the Owl's Roost Tavern, the Magick Emporium and the Wayward Blacksmithe shop.

Aridell is a very small village and we get very few visitors out this way due to the war. You are welcome to stay as long as you'd like. The local merchants are always happy to see a new face in town.
I'm glad to know where I am at, but it doesn't explain how I got here!
Hmm, your situation is very odd indeed

It is regarding honor and justice. It is about reclaiming something that was taken from the people of Thaermore. Three years ago, without reason or provocation, the Orakur chose to undermine centuries of peaceful co-existence with us by stealing the Crux of Ages straight out from under our noses! The Crux- the very spirit of Thaemore- taken as a vagabond would take an apple! Of course, there was a huge public outcry over this event and the Chancellor issued a proclamation stating their actions constituted an act of war. We have been fighting this conflict with them ever since.

The Crux of Ages is Thaermore's most prized artifact; a jewel of absolute perfection and a symbol of Thaermore's majesty. When humans first settled this region long ago The Crux was discovered by miners within a single block of granite. After it was removed from the stone, it became an object of inspiration and power for all of Thaermore. For three hundred years it has rested in a vault in Spire, our capital city, only to be brought out once per year during the summer festivals so that all Thaerish citizens could view it.

Greetings, traveler! I am Eleanor Mistlepine, Council Head here in the village of Aridell. We get very few visitors out this way, so please- if there is anything I can do for you during your stay, please do not hesitate to ask.
Can you answer another question for me?
I need to get going. Thank you.
Of course. Please stop by again if you need anything else.
How can I reach Tangletree Forest from here?
Tangletree Forest is west of here

I no longer know the best way to reach it because I've heard that Grimmhold is impassable. I believe the northern pass is still usable, but that takes you the long way around, around the north end of the forest. That route may be dangerous for I've heard that beasts and bandits roam freely north of here, but you should be safe if you can make it to Darkford.

Yes. three years ago an Orakur agent broke into the vault through a secret tunnel and took it. They took it because they coveted it. From the very day it was found and pulled from the rock, the Orakur claimed ownership of it. This act of theft is an insult to all of Thaermore and the Chancellor has vowed to continue the military action until the jewel is recovered.

Hmm, not much is known about them really. From what I understand they are a race of underground dwelling creatures. Some say they are twisted decedents of the Dwarves, but no one really knows. They are horribly bothered by the sun and never come above ground, even at night because the open air scares them. They thrive in the dark, narrow passages of the underground, surrounded by stone. They rarely fight on their own- they prefer to swarm their enemies with the underground creatures that they seem to hold command over. That is why this land now is so plagued with vile creatures. They use these creatures to wear us down, to drive us from these lands.

Say, I have a book of The History of Thaemore in the drawer beside my desk. You are welcome to take it if you want; it is rather outdated but perhaps there is information in there that can be of help to you.
Thank you for your time. I must be going.

Elderhollow was a casualty of this war that we are currently engaged in. Without any help from the Commonwealth Guard to defend itself, Elderhollow was frequently attacked by Goblins and other creatures that so freely walk the lands now. Most of the town's people left; some settled here, others went north. The few who foolishly stayed paid with their lives.
The tavern owner told me what happened to you.
I know what you're going through. I awoke with no memory of my past or even who I am. I've lost everything as well.

Yeah? Well I'm sorry for your troubles, but that ship and crew were my life. I have nothing without them. Now I'm stranded here in this damn village with no way to return home. All I know how to do is navigate and chart maps; I have no other skill and so there is no work for me here.

To add to my sorrow, I lost my father's sextant in the shipwreck. It was an antique that his father gave to him and he to me. It was a priceless family heirloom. If it's not at the bottom of the sea then it is most certainly in the hands of the thieves that control the Salted Coast area. Either way it's lost forever.
If you're going to drink yourself to death, do it somewhere else. No one cares about your problems.
I'd like to learn more about Cartography now.
If you train in Cartography enough, you'll be able to create detailed maps!
I think found your sextant. Is this it?
By the gods! It is a miracle that you were able to find it. I have absolutely nothing I can give you in exchange for this but my eternal gratitude.
How about you teach me what you know of Cartography?
Really? You want me to teach you Cartography? I might be able to do that for you.

Yeah, I think I can do that. Hey, this can be the start of a new career for me! Of course I'll have to charge you the standard fee for training which is 100 gold per skill level. I feel bad asking you to pay after what you've just done for me, but I must make a living too. I am nearly out of gold and soon even the owner of this tavern will toss me to the street. I can't teach you anything if I am starving and homeless.
That's a deal.
Oh thank you! You've shown me that there are still kind people left in this world. Just return to me when you are ready to learn Cartography.
No way! I risked my life for your damn sextant and you should train me for free.

Well, I regret that is your decision. I haven't had a decent bite to eat nor a warm place to sleep in days. Although I am grateful that you found my sextant, I would probably have to sell it just to keep myself alive.
If you can't afford to give me a little gold for my troubles, I'll have to just sell it myself.
Oh, well you're no better than the thieves in Salted Coast then. Be gone. The sight of you sickens me.
Hail! Welcome to the Owl's Roost Tavern. I'm Porter, the owner. Have a seat! What can I get for you?
So, what can I get for you?
Thanks for spending money at the Owl's Roost Tavern, friend!
Not much news makes it out this way anymore
In fact, I was kinda hoping maybe you had some news for us, you know, with you being from out of town and all.
I'd like to rent a room for the night.
I seem to have lost my memory, so even if I had news to tell you I would have forgotten it!

I'm sorry to hear that, my friend. Why don't you have a drink, or stay for the night here in the Owl's Roost? I might also recommend that you talk to Father Michael over at the Bethel; perhaps you are suffering from an injury that he can help you with.
What's with the sulking man over at the table?

Oh, him? His name is Garrett. Poor guy came in here a month ago and hasn't left. He was a navigator on a ship that was attacked and sank south of Thaermore. He was found unconcious on a beach on Salty Coast. As far as he can tell, he's the only one who made it off the ship alive. He's still in shock about it. He just sits here day and night drinking to forget, I guess.
Thanks for your time, I must be going.
Thank the gods you've arrived! I'm afraid the offensive failed, sir.
You are not with the Commonwealth Guard! Wh..where are our reinforcements?

You must leave. This place is crawling with Goblins. If you make it to Bastion Spire you need to tell them that our attempt to reclaim Grimmhold has failed. The gates remain closed and Grimmhold is not passable.
Is there any way to make Grimmhold passable again?

Perhaps, but you can't do it on your own. <cough> The Goblins destroyed the lever that retracts the gates barricading the Eastern Gap. The only way to open the gates now is to activate the secondary water gate beneath Grimmhold which will...<cough>...will force the gates open. But they infest that area as well. We tried to clear them out but their numbers were too great.
You'll need to take the northern route west.
I'm going to open this water gate and take back Grimmhold myself. Goblins be damned!
Don't be a fool! Six of my Guardsmen couldn't accomplish this feat...I...[cough]
Okay, I'm going back to take the northern route west.
Godspeed to you.
I have been though Grimmhold and have opened the secondary water gates below. Grimmhold is passible again.
You...you did this on your own? Six of my men failed to do this!

I am afraid I do not believe you. You are a fool if you think you can clear the goblins from Grimmhold by yourself. You'll need to take the northern route through Thaermore to go west of here...I...[cough]
What else can I do for you?
I am exploring this area. Is there anything you can tell me about this region?
I know a lot about this area as I've lived here for many years. Is there anything specific you are looking for?
I am here to rob you, wench! Pray I do not take your life as well as your gold.
Oh really? I find it humorous that a pathetic mongrel such as yourself has accidentally chosen to threaten me!
I hope you have enjoyed the life that you've led up 'till now, because it is about to end.
I have been told to locate you and show you this amulet.
This is indeed authentic. Do you not know what this is?
No, I don't. I received a mysterious note telling me that you could identify it for me.
Sure, I can tell you what this amulet is, but it appears that I have the upper hand in this matter
You want information that I possess, and there is a task that I would ask of you. If you perform this job for me, I'll gladly tell you what this amulet is.
I guess I have little choice. Tell me what you need done.
Very good! I knew you were a man of quality judgment.

Well, during your travels through Tangletree you may have noticed unusually large wasps flying about. They are called Hive Drones and they are very aggressive. Their numbers have increased and I believe it is because a Hive Queen has settled somewhere in this area. I need you to find the hive and kill the Hive Queen. When she is gone the Drones will leave this area and search for a new queen. Under any other circumstance my skills with a blade would be more than enough to do the job myself, but it turns out I am extremely allergic to bee stings.
Do this job for me and I will tell you everything you need to know about your amulet.
I don't play games like this. You will tell me what I need to know or I will force it out of you.

Ha! Really? My, you certainly are intimidating, aren't you? Do you have any idea who I am? Of course you don't or you would realize that you are heading towards an ending that I promise you do not want to experience. I'll tell you what- I'll let this one mistake of yours slide and give you another chance to accept my offer.
Yes, okay. I'll take your offer. What is it you want me to do?
No, I don't think *you* have any idea who *I* am!
Well now, this conversation just got interesting...
Excellent! A fews days ago I was searching for mushrooms near Whistling Cave south of here and I ran across a large number Drones. I'm sure the hive is in there.
Return to me with the Queen's stinger and I'll know the task has been completed. Then we will have a talk.
I am not wasting my time killing wasps for you. I grow weary of this conversation. Tell me now what I need to know or there will be hell to pay!
Well hello, what a surprise! I get very few visitors way out here so deep in Tangletree. My name is Lilith. What can I do for you?
I have killed the Hive Queen. Here is her stinger.

Congratulations! That was no easy task, for sure. Any remaining Hive Drones in the area will move on eventually, in search of another Queen. As for the stinger itself, you can keep it. I only needed to see it as proof of your actions.
Now on to the business at hand. Do you still have that amulet with you?
Yes, here it is. [Show the amulet to Lilith]
Alright then
here's what I can tell you about your amulet: it is actually a key. A very special key.
That key of yours will unlock a box in a place called the 'Underground Repository'. Have you heard of it?

Well, it is a special vault designed for people who need a place to store their valuables with no questions asked. It is also very secure. In more than two hundred years since it was built the security of the Repository has never been compromised.

It's more than just a bank. The Underground Repository is a service that provides uncompromised security and anonymity to its members. People who use the Repository are considered part of a secret society who protect other members by upholding a set of strict policies. These people all share two things; the Repository and the code of conduct that goes with it. It is even rumored that the Chancellor himself uses the Repository, though you'll never find anyone who will confirm or deny that.
And this 'amulet key' unlocks a box there?

Yes. This key is paired with a security vault in the Repository. Vault number 26 to be exact, according to the marks across its face. Just show the Vault Master your amulet and you will be allowed to enter and retrieve whatever is stored in the vault. I will warn you now, the management of the Repository have zero tolerance for trespassing or snooping around in general, so do your business and leave.
And where exactly is this Underground Repository located?

Well, unfortunately I can't tell you its exact location, but just go to the town of Blackwater and snoop around a bit. Don't bother to ask anyone about it because nobody there knows anything- well, at least they'll act like they don't know anything. In fact, just talking about it can get you killed, so do the right thing and stay quiet. If you look around long enough, you'll find what you are searching for.
Could you tell me where I could get some supplies?

Personally, I get all my supplies from Bordertown. It's a small camp just half-a-day walk north of here, right outside of Darkford. It's nothing more than a refugee camp, but the merchants there always have what I need.

Southwest of here, outside the forest, is an old mining town called Blackwater. It's a longer walk but worth the journey as the merchants are always well stocked. However, they don't take kindly to refugees and transients, and they require visitors to pay a gate tax to enter the town. They use the money to support their own militia and because of this, Blackwater has fared better than most towns in Thaermore.
That's about it other than Aridell, but that is a couple days walk east of here. The capital, Bastion Spire, has been closed off for quite some time now.
How do you know so much about all this? Have we met before?
No, I have never met you before. However, because you possess that amulet, we share a comradeship.

During my previous profession I acquired several 'assets' which I now store at the Repository. That is all I will say about that. As I said, people who use the Repository share this code of silence. Don't ask about other people's deposits and don't tell others of yours.
I don't have it. I'll get it and bring it back to you.
Thank you for your time, Lilith.
Are there any areas in or around Tanglewood that would be wise for me to know about?

Yes, a word of caution: due west of here is a very dangerous area called Baron's Thicket. There was once a hunting camp owned by Lord Thorndike located there. He kept it stocked with Carniraptors- bipedal reptiles that can strip flesh from bone in seconds. No one tended to the camp after the war began and the Carniraptors have escaped, and they now roam freely throughout Baron's Thicket. I recommend that you do not travel straight west from here.

Beyond Baron's Thicket is a abandoned town named Vela, on the shores of Bottomless Lake. It fell to a Goblin raid over a year ago and is nothing more than a flooded ghost town now. Word is that Goblins still reside there, but I don't travel that way, and the Carniraptors of Baron's Thicket seems to deter them from making their way east.

There's not much south of here. Miles of forest eventually ending on the shores of the Salted Coast. Just a bit southeast of here is Grimmhold, the fortress that once connected the eastern shores with the rest of Thaermore. I've not visited it in more than a year since the guards have abandoned it. Last I heard, it is no longer safe, overrun with Goblins who made their way up from the south along the eastern rift.

If you are interested in a bit of historical sightseeing, there is a preserve just north of here built to protect an old tree. People say the tree is the offspring of the first tree of Tanglewood. I've visited it a couple of times, but I've never seen anything special about it. It just looks like an old tree to me.
I think I've heard enough. Thank you.
I must be going. Thanks for your time.

What can I tell you? I think it is very suspicious, that's what I can tell you. A couple years ago this gem, the 'Crux of Ages', supposedly disappears and the Chancellor declared war with these Orakur creatures that no one seems to know anything about. Soon after that most of Thaermore is overrun with Goblins and all sorts of vermin from the underground. The Chancellor, rather than defend this region, just closes off the all the exit points and leaves everyone here to defend themselves. What kind of war plan is that?
I am one of the lucky ones. I can take care of myself and this forest has protected me fairly well, but the rest of Thaermore may never recover from this war.
Oh human! No harm Gruzz! Me not make war, me be friend!
Greets to you human! Be kind to Gruzz, me be friend!
I do not speak to filth! I am the enemy of all goblins!
Give me one reason why I should not destroy you and then I will determine your fate, goblin.

Ohh, because Gruzz friend of humans. Gruzz not want to be with other goblins when they make war. Something bad going to happen. Gruzz hide here until war end. Spare Gruzz life and he be your friend! Gruzz tell you all he knows!
Tell me what you can about this place.

Oh, this place was for mining. Great gemstone found here! You still find some if you have good eye for hidden things! Gruzz finds lots of gems 'cause Gruzz has good eyes. Now cave filled with giant wasps, they called Hive Drones. Hive Queen is further back. They not bother Gruzz here because Gruzz keep smoky fire. They not like smoke. Gruzz safe.
Gruzz hide here until war over.
Tell me what you know of this war, goblin.

Humans make war with Orakur but something not right. Why human leader let Goblins run around and make trouble? Goblins make war on humans and human leader just ignore them. Something bad going to happen. Gruzz not want to die. Gruzz hide here until all over.
Powerful shaman named Gramuk is leading goblin clans now. Clans move across Thaermore looking for great gemstone. Not know what happens next.

Gruzz knows nothing! Gruzz never see Orakur. Human soldiers far away chasing shadows. Goblin shaman Gramuk spreading vermin to weaken humans. Humans blame Orakur for this, not Goblins! Gruzz not be part of war. Great suffering coming to all.
Shhh, Gramuk may be listening! Gramuk see people with his mind. Maybe Gruzz say too much. No more talk or Gramuk may find Gruzz and human.

Gruzz say you welcome. Gruzz thank human for not harming Gruzz, so Gruzz tell you secret! Gruzz used to be in charge of cleaning weapons in Goblin Citadel. If you ever get captured and taken to Citadel, maybe you can escape! Maybe you can use powerful weapon for help.
There be a lock box in Citadel, near where Goblins keep prisoners. The box lock need be set to 66 and then box open. Powerful weapon there!
I have no further use for you, goblin. Prepare to die!
What can you tell me of this war, goblin?
Thank you. Perhaps that information may be useful to me someday.
Sounds fair. Here is 100 gold pieces.
Greetings Traveler.
Open the gates. I have business to do in your town.
Is that right? Have you been cleared?

As a way of maintaining security here in our fine city and to keep out riffraff and vagrants,  the mayor requires a one time gate tax of 100 gold pieces. Pay the tax and the gates to Blackwater will always be open to you. If you can't pay the tax, you cannot enter the town.
Sounds fair. Here's is 100 gold pieces.
Thank you. You may enter the city.
Then you will not pass. Be gone before I gut you like a fish.
Greetings to you, guest of Blackwater. I am Eeru, owner of The Lonely Spirits Tavern. Relax and have a drink! I have a room available if you need a bed for the night.
What can I do for you?
I'd like to see what you have for sale.
Thank you very much for shopping with us.
Certainly! I have a fine room available.
What name will you be staying under?
Ah, yes. Let me escort you personally to your room. When you are finshed resting, just pull the lever to ring the bell. I will come and get you again.
Hail traveler! Come here! My name is Erik and this is my metalshop here in Bordertown. Please, let me to show you some of my stock.
You want to see what else I have for sale? You'll find no better selection than mine.
Yes, I'd like to look at your inventory.
Can you tell me a bit about this village?

We've been calling this camp 'Bordertown'. Most of the people here, myself included, were forced to leave their homes elsewhere in Thaermore because of this damn war. We've all traveled north, hoping to pass through Darkford and reach the western lands. Unfortunately, Darkford has been closed by the Chancellor and the guards are not letting anyone through. So, we've all just made temporarily homes here waiting for the Chancellor to allow people to pass west again. It's been over a year now and we're still waiting.
Unfortuantely I am a bit short on gold. Do you have any work for me?

I might have something for you but the job is really tough! Gunther, the metal smith down in Blackwater, has ordered a smelting crucible from me and I have not found any way to deliver it to him. See, the problem is that it weighs 70 pounds!

After the war began all the horses in Thaermore were gathered up to be used in military service, so there's really no other way to get this down to him other than for someone to carry it. I figured that someone a strong back or perhaps a keen sense of magick could think up with an ingenious way of transporting it down there. Maybe you're just the guy I am looking for.
Before you just agree to it, remember that it weighs 70 pounds. If you sucessfully get it to Gunther, he will pay you 600 gold. It's a big job with big pay!

Darkford is the stronghold that secures Azure pass through Barrier Range, which separates the eastern and western lands of Thaermore. It's really the quickest and safest route west towards Bastion Spire, the capital of Thaermore.
Until Darkford is opened or this war comes to an end, we are all just stuck here.
You seem to be making the best of your situation here.

Yes, I suppose so. The Captain at Darkford occasionally orders supplies from me and I do a lot of work maintaining the soldiers weapons, not to mention supplying travelers such as yourself. Yeah, I'd say I do more business here than I ever did in Vela. Still, I'd gladly give it up to be able to head home again.

The same thing that has happened to many of the other towns and villages across Thaermore. After the start of the war, we began defending ourselves against Salamanders and Bloodsippers, supposedly sent from the underworld by the Orakur. This wasn't much more than a nuisance to us, but then the Goblins showed up. They came from Crakamir; made their way up the Nimmia River in huge numbers. We held them off as long as possible, but then those bastards broke the levee that held back the waters of Bottomless Lake. Vela was flooded and the survivors fled.
The Chancellor says the Goblins are not a concern, but he obviously has no idea what we're up against out here.

Great! The crucible is over in the chest next to the furnace. It's not very big, but it is made of dense ceramic and it is very heavy. Remember to lift with your legs when you pick it up or you'll throw your back out! Good luck!
I am interested in the job, but I must prepare myself first. When I am capable of carrying 70 pounds for that distance, I will return to you.
That's the spirit! Just come back and ask me about the job again when you are ready.
That's not for me. I may be a lot of things but I'm not a pack mule.
That's okay. I didn't think you had it in you but I figured I'd tell you about the job anyways. If you have any friends that can do it, send 'em my way.
Halt. Darkford is closed. No one may pass without clearance from the Chancellor.
I have important business to attend to in the west. Let me pass!
Show me your writ from the Chancellor and I'll let you pass. If you have no writ then I suggest you leave or there will be hell to pay.
I have a letter I must show the captain. I have evidence that a priest in Aridell is aiding the goblins on some scheme to create a portal!
Do you now? Well, that sounds really important. I guess the Captain should just put this entire war on hold so you can show him your little letter!
Listen, you maggot. I have information regarding a possible invasion by the goblins. If you prevent me from notifying the Captain about this and it happens, you are going to hang. This I promise.

Alright then. You go straight in and stay to the left. If the Captain is busy you just set the letter on his table and leave. If you are caught doing anything else but delivering this letter, I will cut your feet off myself.
Perhaps you could deliver it to the Captain for me?
We have been horribly short of toiletry paper, so yes, I'd gladly take your letter and put it to good use. Hand it over then!
Here it is.
Oh, why thank you!
We had beans again for breakfast and I'm going to be needing this a bit later!

Hail my friend! Come in, come in. My name is Gunther, owner of this here metal shop. I buy and sell weapons and armor so please feel free to have a look at my inventory. It truly is the best you'll find in all of Thaermore.
You needin' any weapons or armor? Gunther will help you out!
Yes, I'd like to have a look at your inventory.

Well, we're fairly secure here in our town, but outside the city walls it's rather dangerous from what I hear. For example, Vela, a port city just north of here, fell to a Goblin raid a while back. Criminals and creatures of all sorts run wild out there.

I've even heard rumors that the Goblins have brought in Taurax from the far south to help them overtake Thaermore! Do you know what a Taurax is, son? It's a seven foot tall half-bull, half man abomination! They say that a few were spotted just a mile away at the site of the old Loneloft ruins! I think we can defend ourselves against almost anything but an army of Taurax and a throng of Goblins may be too much!
I hope it doesn't come to that. I hope the Chancellor sends troops soon to help us with security.
Do you have any work that needs done? I'm always looking to put a bit more gold in my pocket.

Well, yes, I do need something but it isn't going to be an easy task. You see, I had purchased a bit of Divine Ore from Farwick in Aridell a few months ago. On route for delivery, it was stolen by a band of Mercenaries who have a hideout somewhere east of here. I don't know if they still have it or if they sold it, but if you are as tough as you look, maybe you could 'convince' them to do the right thing and give it back
I paid a lot of money for that little bit of Ore. If you find it, I'll pay you the full value of what it's worth to have it back.
I have with me a ceramic crucible that Erik of Bordertown asked me to bring you.
Good god son! You carried this damn thing all the way from Bordertown on your back!?
Well, Erik had set the delivery charge on this thing at 600 gold, so I guess you're the man who gets it. Here you go, you deserve every bit of it!
Yes, I will find this Divine Ore for you.
You are quite the adventurous type! Well, I wish you the very best success! I'll be here when you find it.
No, I don't mess around with Mercenaries.
Heh, I don't blame you! Oh well, I guess I should just get over my loss.
I have brought back your Divine Ore.
Yep, that's it! Thank you very much! Now then, I believe I owe you 500 gold for this, don't I?
There you go! And thanks again, you've been a real help!

Greetings to you! My name is Leurik. I am the director of Eversleep Cemetery. I assume you have come to inquire about funeral services for a loved one, or perhaps you wish to make arrangements for yourself?
Are you ready to make arrangements for yourself and your love ones for when that unfortunate day comes?
Perhaps. Could you tell me more about Eversleep Cemetery?

Certainly! Eversleep Cemetery is located due west of here and it is the finest resting grounds in all of eastern Thaermore. We handle all the details of the funeral and have an assortment of coffins, caskets, and private vaults to suit your needs. We offer traditional ground burials as well as internment within our private crypt where your loved ones can rest safely until the very end of time. Do you desire cremation? No problem! Embalmment? Our pleasure! I'll personally see to it that the needs of you and your family are taken care of.
Why don't we begin the paperwork now to secure a spot for you and your loved ones?
I need to retrieve something that belongs to me.

I find that a bit hard to believe. You look as though you're nothing more than a common adventurer, and people such as yourself think nothing of looting the dead. Life is just a big adventure to you, isn't it? Well I...

I'll tell you what. This is not something I would normally do, but these are not normal times now, are they? I happen to have a bit of a problem downstairs in my basement. It is full of Salamanders. If you were to go down there and clear the basement out, I would gladly give you a key to the crypt as payment for your services. Deal?
My business is my own. Give me the key.
Well with that I do believe you've exhausted your welcome. Please remove yourself from my house at once!

Splendid! Just head into the basement and get to work. Be careful! Don't let them surround you or you'll be in trouble. You can always come back upstairs if you need to take a break; they won't follow you. When there's nothing left down there, come talk to me again.
I am not an exterminator. Give me the key or I will find a way to get it myself.
I've given you a very generous offer and this is how you respond? You have exhausted your welcome. Please leave my house at once!
About that salamander problem in your basement...
Ah, not right now. Thanks for your time.

I'd like to check out the quality of your crypt before committing to anything. An eternity is a very long time to have to lie in an unsatisfactory tomb. May I have a key to unlock the crypt so I may take a peek inside?

I'm sorry but we have had quite a problem with vandalism recently and I cannot give a key to just anyone. Perhaps with a small non-refundable deposit put towards your intent to purchase a plot I will know you are serious, and then I will give you a key to the vault. 200 gold pieces would be a sufficient deposit I suppose.
Yes, that is acceptable. Here is 200 gold.
Thank you! We appreciate your interest in our services. Please, go look at our facilities and come back when you are ready to make your arrangements.
I'm sorry to hear that. Well, we do offer pauper burials as well. There is no shame in putting yourself or your dear mother in a leaky pine box if that is all you can afford.
Why it appears they are! Well, a deal is a deal. Take this key. You may retrieve whatever object you claim is yours and then promptly leave.
Well keep at it. You'll get no key from me if you can't clean up my problem downstairs!
I need a key to enter the main crypt in Eversleep Cemetery.
Oh, really now? What reason would a person such as yourself have to enter my private crypt except to rob the dead of their valuables?
No thanks. I don't plan on dying anytime soon.
Greetings. I am the Vault Master here at the Repository. I hope for your sake you have the proper authorization to be here. Show it to me now, human.
Show me your authorization, human.
Just a moment, human.
Here is my key.
You may pass human.
Perhaps this is what you are looking for?
Hmm, yes, this is a passkey for vault number 26. Go about your business but do not fail to obey the house rules, human.
I have this key.
Um, I think I will just show myself out.

Oh, you startled me! I thought you were one of those wretched cutpurse thugs that are always trying to sneak in here. My name is Paul. I don't know who you are or what you want, but I warn you- I am sick. You best not stay long or you're likely to catch what I've got.
I recommend you don't stay too long...you may catch what I've got.
Greetings. I am just passing through and hoped that you could chat with me a bit about this region.

Sure. I don't see many travelers pass through here anymore so I'll be happy to chat for a bit. This area is called the Salted Coast because twice per year the tides rise extra high and floods most of the lowlands south of here. The soil along the shoreline is so salted that nothing grows well.

It used to be quite a nice place to live, actually. Just a few years ago I spent my days gathering salt and growing herbs to sell in Elderhollow. Then the war came and any sense of law and order disappeared. Now I spend what days I have left just defending my home from the thieves that roam this area. That's what my 'blast barrier' is for, so if any of those bastards try to get near here I'll send 'em all to their grave!
I am here to rob you. Hand over your valuables!
My valuables? Are you serious? Yeah, sure have at it. Take all the 'valuables' you can find.
I've gotten infected with a disease called Fleshrot. It'll kill me eventually, if the murderous thugs in the area don't get me first.
I don't think there is anything I can do about it. I've tried countless remedies and potions, but the disease has progressed too far. I am just trying to stay comfortable for what time I have left.

I really don't know anything about it. One day everything is fine, the next day all hell broke loose! The Commonwealth Guards who are supposed to be maintaining law just up and disappeared. I guess they were called into service to fight the war with the Orakur, but in their absence this place has fallen into chaos. I even heard that Grimmhold was overrun by Goblins! Well, with my illness I am not long for this world, so I guess I really don't care much about what happens, honestly.
Heh, yeah. I've used it a couple times too. Doesn't leave much to clean up but fragments of bone.
Father Michael, you say?
You damn fool! That was not a healing elixir! When have you ever known a healing elixir to look and smell like boiled-down Noximander venom?
I was just trying to help. I didn't know.

Father Michael is the person responsible for infecting me with this disease, vile piece of Troll dung that he is. Apparently he is upset that it hasn't killed me yet and was hoping the poison would finish me off.
See, I know things. I know he is involved with the Goblins somehow.

Well, a few months ago there was a messenger passing through the Salted Coast area heading to Aridell. He was attacked by thugs down near the shoreline and was killed, and when I found his body there was a letter floating in the water nearby. The saltwater had broken the seal on the letter and I saw that it was for Father Michael from a Goblin named 'Gramuk'. It was instructions for finishing a portal to allow Goblins to travel to the Darkford region.

When Father Michael heard that I recovered his 'sealed letter' he sent someone to retrieve it. He also sent me a whole salted ham to show his appreciation for my efforts in securing the letter. But within a day of eating some of the meat I was stricken with this horrible disease. Apparently the Father wanted to make sure I hadn't accidently read anything that might incrimiate him.
So why would father Michael be involved with Goblins?
I don't know. All I know is that I actually kept the original letter. What I sent back to him was something I copied by hand and, well, changed a few of the instructions around.
I was able to restick the wax seal on the fake letter so that it looked legitimate. There's no way the portal will ever work with the instructions I gave him!

Look, if you really want to help me, take this original letter to someone in charge, someone who has the power to bring father Michael to justice. Don't show this to anyone in Aridell; they all think Father Michael is some sort of damned saint. They won't believe what I've told you. Take it north to Darkford and show it to the Captain who oversees operations there. He's probably the highest in authority remaining in this area of Thaermore.
Yes, I believe you. I will do this task.

Thank you! I am glad to have this off my shoulders. Take the note and give it to the Captain at Darkford. You may need to convince the Guards to let you in, but I'm sure he will be very interested to hear about Father Michael's actions.

By the way, I think the portal Father Michael is working on is somewhere near Darkford. I've heard that he owns a cottage up there where he frequently visits, spending many hours engaged in 'theological study'.
No, I don't believe your story and I will not do this task.
That is fine. I figured no one would believe my story. Anyways, I do not have a lot of time left and I guess I don't really care what happens to this place after I am gone.
Good day to you.
Whether or not I believe you is irrelevant. I really don't care either way and I've got better things to do with my time. [END]

Hello traveler. I am Krista, owner of this make-shift tavern here in Bordertown. I have a few items to eat or drink if you're hungry and I offer many other items for sale that that I've acquired from people passing through.
What can I get for you?
I am looking for a woman named Lilith. I was told she lives somewhere in Tangletree Forest. Have you heard of her?
Hmm, yes, I know of Lilith. She comes here every few weeks to pick up supplies. She lives just south of here, near Lake Atria, not more than half-a-day's walk.

I'm not completely familiar with this area actually; I'm just a refugee like everyone else here. I know that just east of here is a huge stronghold that people call Shadowmirk. It's a centuries old refuge for a cult of eclectic Mages. No one really knows much about them but I am always fascinated by the structure when I am out that way gathering herbs from the swamps.
Which reminds me: stay clear of that area unless you know what you are doing. It is infested with Fungal Slimes!
I'm looking for some work. Got anything?

Well, perhaps. I have been hoping to find someone who would be willing to go to Grimmhold and retrieve an item for me. You see, my brother was once a soldier stationed at Grimmhold; he was a lieutenant actually. He kept with him a family locket that our mother had given to him for good luck while he was serving in the Commonwealth Guard.

When the Chancellor called all the available guards into service, he packed up and shipped out within hours. He left behind a few belongings, the locket being one of them. Now, it isn't worth much, but it has significant sentimental value to both of us. Since Grimmhold has been overrun with Goblins, I am more concerned than ever that we may never get it back. I would pay you a couple hundred gold if you are able to find the locket and bring it back to me.

Really? That's great! Okay then, I have something to give you. It is a key to my brother's quarters; he left it with me when passing through on his way west hopeful that I may have the chance to retrieve it in case he never returned. The locket should be in a chest or cabinet in his room. I don't know where his quarters where located, but you'll obviously know it when you find the lock that this key fits.
I can't do it. Grimmhold is in the opposite direction from where I am heading.
That's okay, I'll keep searching for someone. Perhaps even I could buy some equipment from Erik the blacksmith and head down there myself.
I think I found the locket. Is this it?
Oh, yes it is! Thank you, thank you, thank you! I can't express how happy I am to see this locket again.
Well, as promised, here is 200 gold. Thank you again!

Hail stranger! My name is Gamfari. I am a herbalist and alchemist here in Bordertown. I spend most of my free time walking the countryside gathering rare reagents. I can promise you that you'll find no better assortment of alchemy supplies north of Darkwater!
Care to see my stock, or how about a lesson in Alchemy?
Needing any herbs or alchemy supplies? Or how about a quick lesson in mixing techniques?
I would like to learn a bit about Alchemy.
Thank you for inquiring about Alchemy lessons.
Come and see me anytime you need Alchemy supplies. I have the best stock in Thaermore!
Brother? Brother! Is...is that you?
You did it. You drank the serum and you've forgotten who I am. I am thankful you did it brother or you would be hanging in the rack next to me already.

I am sorry you do not remember me brother. You did what you had to do to protect yourself, but since you are here I must tell you what I've overheard the goblins talking about. Listen to me now before life escapes me,
Yes, it is me. I drank a serum and lost my memory, but I left myself a note to find you!
Brother, you...you shouldn't have written yourself a note. We discussed the dangers of that! What if they find you?
Brother, I wish our final meeting could have been under other circumstances, but before life escapes me I must tell you what I've heard the goblins talking about.

The goblins are scheming something big. I've heard them speak of taking over all of Thaermore. They speak of a goblin shaman named Gramuk. He has taken control of the Chancellor's mind which is why Thaermore is undefended.
Brother, they will find you soon. Whether you posses the Crux or not, they are going to find you and your fate will be the same as mine.

There is little time left. The goblins speak of destroying Shadowmirk, the Mage Citadel to the north. There's a wizard who resides there named Erubor. They fear him and want him eliminated. Go to Shadowmirk and find Erubor. Tell him what I've told you. If Shadowmirk falls, so shall the remainder of Thaermore.
What of the Crux of Ages? What are they saying about it?

Th...the Crux? Please brother, say not another word! If you possess it, do not tell me. Anything you say to me may be heard by Gramuk. If you do have it, keep it close to you for it may offer some sort of protection. It was the removal of the Crux from Bastion Spire that allowed Gramuk to gain control of the Chancellor's mind. I do not know what else to tell you of it. Perhaps you can seek Erudor advice on the matter, but only if you trust him.
Now, there is one thing I must ask of you, brother,
Brother, end my life. I...I am broken. Even with the most powerful of medicines I cannot recover from this. I will be dead in a few hours...please do not allow me to suffer that long.
I am sorry you do not remember me brother, but I am glad the amnesia will spare you the pain of my passing.
I will do this for you. Goodbye, brother.
I cannot do what you ask of me.
Hail to you, traveler. My name is Mary. If...if you are a bandit come to rob me I must tell you your friends paid a visit not more than 2 days ago. They've taken everything I had. There is no more.
I'm not here to rob you. Do you need any help?

Well, I guess if you are offering, perhaps you could locate my husband Bradon. We were traveling north to Darkford when our wagon broke. I set up camp here and tended to our belongings while he went ahead to get parts. That was nearly a week ago and Darkford should have only been a three-day walk there and back. I fear the worst has happened.
Unfortunately for you I am, in fact, here to rob you. I'm sure I can find something worth taking.
I will not resist so please to not harm me. Take what you want and leave.
Yes, I could try to locate him for you.

Oh thank you so much! As I said, my husband's name is Bradon. Please tell him to hurry back here even if he has not found the wagon parts yet. At this point we have no more belongings to haul and I'm starting to use the wagon for firewood.

If you find...I mean, if something has happened to him, you may be able to identify him by his wedding band. We were married just last spring and it has not left his finger since that day. It's just a simple gold ring inscribed with my name.
No, I have no time to track down lost husbands. I'm sure he'll show up eventually.
Very well. Thank you anyways. Now if you'll excuse me I have work to do.
I found a dead man with this ring in his possession. I'm sorry.
Whether or not the deceased man who possessed this ring was Bradon, something awful must have befallen him for him to give this ring up.
Thank you for this, but I have nothing to offer you for your help.

Wait, I can give you some information that you may benefit from. Just west of Grimmhold, deep in Tangletree Forest, there is an abandoned house that belonged to my father. In this house is a chest that contains a valuable weapon. The chest is nearly unbreakable and can only be opened by setting the slider lock to number 167. If you locate the house and the chest, you can have the weapon inside. Consider it payment for what you have done for me.
Thank you. I will look for this chest.
Thank you very much for your patronage.
I'm looking to earn some gold. Do you have any tasks that I could do for you?

As a matter of fact, I do have something that you could help me with. I was just speaking to the town council head and we were discussing the disappearance of the Burley Oak tree from this region. It used to grow plentiful in the southern area of Tangletree Forest, but it seems that the spreading population of Acid Grubbs has taken to stripping the bark from the trees which has killed them all.

I've heard that there is a single tree left somewhere in the far southern area of Tangletree Forest. I would like to get an acorn from this Burley Oak before it is killed as well. We will then try to cultivate it here in Blackwater and save the species from extinction.
I can pay you a small fee for your service if you were to bring this acorn back.
Great! Just bring the acorn back to me when you find it.
Oh, okay. Well you asked if I had any jobs and that is all I have right now.
I have brought back the acorn you wanted.
Thank you so much! We will get this acorn planted right away. It may take 30 years, but eventually this tree will produce acorns of its own.
Oh, and here is a bit of gold for your reward.
Welcome back, blessed traveler. What can I do for you?
Welcome to the Basilica of Saint Velhera. My name is Father Jonathon. Here at the Basilica we can heal your wounds and restore your soul, for a small donation of course.
We also offer spiritual training, for those looking to spread the word of Saint Velhera. Divination is a powerful ally in the war against evil.
I would like to know more about Divination.
Psst! Come over here. I would like to have a word with you.
You look like just the type of person I've been searching for. I have a job offer for you. It's a simple job with a big paycheck.
I am looking for someone to help me with a problem. There is an individual who has become troublesome to me and must be eliminated. Are you interested in the job?
There is a woman who resides in Tangletree Forest. Her name is Lilith and she lives in a cottage on Lake Atria. The reasons I want her killed are my own and do not concern you.

Hear this, for it is most important: she wears an amulet around her neck. It is just a worthless trinket and is of no importance to me, of course. However, I need that amulet returned to me to prove you have completed the task. I can assure you she won't part with it while she is still breathing.
If you do this job, I will pay you 500 gold and may have other work for you. So, are you interested?
Very well. I thought you looked as if this was your type of job.
So this conversation never took place then, right?
Yes, I will do this job. I will return with her amulet.
That's the spirit! I will wait here for you. Remember, you get the money only when you bring back the amulet.
Oh yes, and be careful. She is very dangerous. Don't toy with her, just end her life as quickly as possible.
I know of Lilith and I consider her to be a friend! I will not let you carry out this job. Prepare to die!
Well, well. I wasn't sure you would be capable of completing this task,
A deal is a deal, even among us unscrupulous.
Now leave. We never had this conversation.
Greetings again, human. How goes your quest?

Human, please approach! I am Oolaseph and I am the direct descendant of the very first tree to take root here more than ten millennia past. That tree, my greatest grandfather, was the first tree in what your people would later call Tanglewood Forest.

I feel grave times are approaching for our kind, both the race of men and trees. I have seen goblins moving through the moonlight. I have heard my brethren speak of the coming war. I speak to you now because I would like to offer you help.
A talking tree wants to help me? How do you know of me?

My brethren- my fellow tree kin- have spoken of you. They have seen your travels. They have seen you smite that which is attacking the land. They have told me you can help defeat this engine of destruction, this coming storm.

I have not seen this for myself because my roots are not connected with theirs. I have been isolated here on this small parcel of earth so that I am protected from plague and fire if it were to overtake my brethren. It is critical that my lineage does not end, least it be the end of all trees in Thaermore.

And so for my continued protection and that of my brethren, I would like to offer you help in the form of a gift. However, before I could give this gift to you, you must first prove your worth. If you can perform a difficult task for me, I will grant you one gift of the tree kin to aid you in your efforts. What say you?
I will not listen to these voices in my head! Be gone!

In northwest Crakamir, the barren lands far to the south, there is a small oasis. Located there is a well, and within the well is water so pure it is unlike anything else in this world. It is water that has filtered through sand and rocks for a thousand years, and it percolates up from the cool underground to that very spot. But now the goblins have captured the oasis and they have placed terrible beasts there to guard it. Their plan is to pollute the water source which will have far reaching effects on every plant and animal and person in Thaermore.
I ask that you bring me a flask of water from the oasis. If we can keep just one vial of Purest Water from being polluted we can use it to restore the oasis when the Goblin scourge ends.
I will do this. I will return with your water.

Very good. I do not wish for you to be sent to your death, so please be confident that you are skilled enough to endure the dangers of Crakamir before undertaking my quest. This task is not for the weak nor ill prepared. Many before you have died attempting to reach this oasis.
I need not prove my worth to a tree, and I will certainly not fetch you water as if I were your gardener!
That is regretful, human. I have made a poor choice to offer help to the race of men. It will not happen again.
I have returned with your water!
Very good, human! I am pleased that you have completed this task. You have proven your worth to me and I will now give you the gift that I spoke of.

One hundred years ago a great Ranger named Lorus of Eastleaf died after a lifetime of protecting this forest. His legendary bow was made from one of my branches and was buried with him. You have my permission to retrieve his bow and use it towards your crusade. If you are unskilled in archery, you may sell it to acquire funds to purchase items that will help you.
His tomb is located in Tangletree Ossuary. His vault is secured with a sliding lock. To release the lock set the slider to 98. Be warned, anything else will trigger a deadly trap!
Go now, human. Fight the Goblins and end this scourge!

Well, well! What 'ave we here? Looks to me like this rat was trying to pass through our forest without paying the road tax. Don't you know this 'ere road belongs to us, rat? We don't take kindly to filthy varmin who think they can just walk anywhere they want.
Stand back you pathetic mongrels, least I deliver all of you to your fates!
Ha ha! You hear that boys?! This foul little rat is threatening our lives, and I don't believe he 'as any intention of paying the tax.
This one needs to learn some respect, he does. What do ya say we open this varmin's gut right 'ere and hang 'em from a tree, eh?
After him, boys! Cut the rat's throat!
If this is your land then it is only proper that I should pay a tax for passing through.
Ah! There, you see boys? This one knows what's good for him.
The tax for using our road is 75 gold. You pay this and you can be on your merry little way. If you don't 'ave it...well, eh, lets just 'ope you do!
Yes, 75 gold is a resonable tax. Here you go.
I will not pay this ridiclous 'road tax'. It is time I be on my way.
Oh, uh, you startled me! My name is Walter. I have just joined the acolytes here in Shadowmirk and I'm working on my first assignment. Are you an initiate here too?
Well, I guess we have the same first assignment: finding out how to get up to level two of the tower.

Look, I don't want to get into any trouble so stop talking to me. And where is your robe and hat? I wouldn't want to be in your shoes if a senior acolyte catches you walking around in that attire! Now please leave me alone. If we try to help each other we will both fail and be thrown out!
No, I am just an adventurer. I found my way inside and am just looking around.

Really? And you made it past the Dimensional Eye that guards the front gates? I am impressed! Still, you're probably not going to find much here other than a lot of trouble. The senior acolytes above don't take kindly to outsiders wandering through Shadowmirk!
I am not an initiate. I must speak to a mage named Erubor. Heard of him?

Ha! Erubor? Of course I've heard of him. He is the headmaster here at Shadowmirk. I mean, I've never actually talked to him or even seen him, but I know he lives at the top of this tower. Good luck getting to talk to him. Most acolytes study for years in this place before they get to speak with the headmaster...and you're not even an initiate!
Can you tell me a bit about Shadowmirk?

Shadowmirk is a puzzling tower of tricks and riddles and traps, as well as a school and research library for all acolytes looking to become grand mages. Generally you are only allowed in by invitation.

I was just recently admitted to Shadowmirk and so I am called an initiate. I am here on the lowest level and must find a way to level two, which is a test that shows I am ready for further training. However, at the moment I am not doing so well. I was just in the Arachnid chamber and I dropped the key to the Necrotic studies lab while trying to collect silk from an egg sack. I'm too drained right now to retrieve it so I am just going to rest for a while before going back in.
If you're going to be wandering around Shadowmirk you had better have your wits about you!

Well, I can't help you with any of the puzzles you may encounter because I haven't seen them myself yet, but I've heard they range from simple riddles to certain death! They are designed to test your intelligence and skills with magick.

Now then, I am sorry if I sound rude, but I must get back to the assignment. If you continue to walk around here and get caught, don't mention my name or I could get thrown out. In fact, please don't bother me again!
What can you tell me about this place?
Are you prepared to leave?

Ehem. Good day, citizen! I am Captain Morgan, head of Darkford. I'm not sure what reason the guards had to let you in but I'll tell you I'm not too pleased. We have a strict policy against any non-military personnel in Darkford. So tell me, what is this reason you are here, citizen?
Captain, I have a letter I must give you. It is incriminating evidence that the priest in Aridell is plotting something with the goblins.
Here, let me take a look at that.

Yes. I see what you mean. Well then, very good citizen. I will forward this to the office of the Chancellor and they will investigate your claim post haste. This will be all we will need of you. I trust you can find your way out.
Wait. That's your response? Something must be done about this immediately!
I said it would be dealt with.
There now, you've served your country and you have been rewarded. It is time you leave before you are arrested. Good day to you.

Welcome $, please approach. I am honored to have finally met you. I am Erubor, the person with whom you've come to see. I am glad that Shadowmirk wasn't an overwhelming challenge for you, though I didn't think it would be.
Please tell me why you have come all this way.
I am simply here exploring. I don't know anything about you and I certainly was not looking for you.

Is that really all you are doing? Well, then, please continue. I happen to be a very powerful mage and I can view the past and the present, though the future is harder to see. However, I have forseen your arrival. I know there are things much greater than you realize happening to you. You must continue the journey you are on and I will not stand in your way, so long as your actions are peaceful.
Erubor, I've come here to tell you that Shadowmirk is in danger.

Yes, yes. This I know. The goblins, they are on the move. I have seen these events unfold. Like the ancient Mystics, I can view the past and the present, though the future is harder to see. I have forseen your arrival and I have seen the goblins plotting against Shadowmirk, but the outcome of these events I cannot predict.
What will happen if Shadowmirk falls to the goblins?

If Shadowmirk falls, so shall the rest of Thaermore. Shadowmirk is Thaermore's last defense since the Chancellor is no longer well. He is under a wicked spell placed upon him by the Goblin shaman Gramuk. He believes the Orakur stole the Crux of Ages and so he has sent his men-at-arms far away, deep underground, to chase shadows. This has left the goblins free to run amok, unchallenged.

The hex that has befallen the Chancellor occured because the Crux was removed from Bastion Spire. The Crux grants wisdom to those who are in its presence, and without that protection the Chancellor has had his thoughts twisted upon the lies that Gramuk has fed him.

We must see to it that the Crux of Ages is recovered and returned to Bastion Spire; it is the only way to break Gramuk's hold on the Chancellor's mind. Unfortunately, I can't say where the Crux is located, but I know that you are connected to it in some way. You must keep searching if you are to find it. Look for clues in your past and it may lead you to the Crux.
Even after you recover the Crux, returning it to Bastion Spire will not be as easy as walking it up to the front gates.

Yes, $, this I know as well. It offers you the protection that it once offered the Chancellor. Keep it with you at all cost. You are its caretaker until it can be returned to Bastion Spire, which is a task you must undertake. It is the only way to break Gramuk's hold on the Chancellor's mind.

This will be difficult because there is no way into Bastion Spire. All entrances and exits have been sealed off, except for one: a portal within the Goblin Citadel which was originally used to steal the Crux. Gramuk keeps the portal secure for when the Commonwealth Guard is too weakened to challenge him, then he will invade Bastion Spire with full force.

$, against all odds, you must go to the Goblin Citadel and use this portal to return the Crux to Bastion Spire. Unfortunately, you have few other options. You are a hunted man. Gramuk is using all his agents to locate you because of your involvement with the Crux.
Listen carefully, for now I will tell you how to enter the Goblin Citadel.

There are four Goblin Keys needed to enter the Citadel. They were placed in the ownership of four Goblin warlords, and only with all four keys recovered can you enter the Citadel. Fortunately, these warlords have done a poor job protecting them and I know of two keys that have already slipped from their possession.

I have one of these keys which I will give to you now. This key was recently recovered by a Ranger Lord of Tanglewood and given to me to protect. It is certainly one of the reasons Gramuk wants to see Shadowmirk torn apart brick by brick. The key is in the chest next to my bed,

As for the other two keys, they are still somewhere in Thaermore. Perhaps you have even recovered them already. If not, look for where the goblins have begun to gather and most likely a warlord is leading them. Kill the warlord and recover the key. When you have recovered all four keys and the Crux, it is time to enter the Citadel and deal with Gramuk.

Yes, of course. You may take anything else that is in my bedroom chest that you find helpful. As well, I will do my best to keep the goblins preoccupied. As long as they are fixated on Shadowmirk and myself, they will not be expecting a lone person to enter the Citadel.
I have faith in you, my boy. Together we may be able to stop this goblin scourge. Go now without further delay. When you are ready to leave Shadowmirk, exit through the portal in the southwest room.
Why would this be such a difficult task?
Erubor, what can you tell me about this war?

It's a complicated matter really. You see, the Chancellor of Thaermore has been bewitched. He is under a powerful spell set by the Goblin shaman Gramuk. Gramuk has fooled the Chancellor into thinking that the Orakur have taken the Crux of Ages, but it is the Goblins who have stolen the gem and subsequently lost it. Now the Goblins are looking for it once again, and the Commonwealth Guards have been sent far away to fight the Orakur.

I know very little about them actually. I do know that they exist, but I doubt they are a threat to anyone. Gramuk has planted this idea in the Chancellor's mind that the Orakur are responsible for the theft of the Crux. Because so little is known about the Orakur it was easy for the people of Thaermore to rally behind the false accusation, even when no evidence supports it. To the common person the Orakur represents all that is dark and sinister. People fear what they do not know, and so the mystery of the Orakur appears to be a far greater threat than the ongoing Goblin scourge.
